Jawline
JAW-lyne
noun (Gen Alpha slang)
An ordinary English compound (jaw + line) for the outline of the lower face, made a fixation by the looksmaxxing culture of the late 2010s and 2020s, which treats a sharp, square jaw as the master key to male attractiveness. Gen Alpha boys post "jawline checks," practice mewing (a tongue-posture technique claimed to reshape the jaw), chew hard silicone jaw-trainers, and turn their heads in photos to show the angle; "his jawline is crazy" is high praise and "no jawline" a taunt.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

In Gen Alpha talk, a good jawline is one of the most important things a boy can have — sharp, square, "mogging" the other guys. Boys as young as ten post jawline pictures, practice mewing, and worry that their faces are not good enough. The Christian observation: Scripture says plainly that God is not impressed by the things we measure in mirrors. "He delighteth not in the strength of the horse: he taketh not pleasure in the legs of a man. The LORD taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy" (Psa 147:10-11). The Messiah Himself, in Isaiah’s portrait, had "no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him" (Isa 53:2) — the most important face in history was not a jawline face. Caring for the body is good — "bodily exercise profiteth little" (1Ti 4:8), and little is not nothing — but a boy who studies his jaw more than his heart is training for the wrong contest. A father can tell a five-year-old son: "God made your face just right. What He cares about most is your heart — are you kind, are you brave, do you love Him?" And to the twelve-year-old: "The LORD taketh pleasure in them that fear him" — that is the measurement that counts.

Webster 1828 Definition

Ordinary word for the lower face’s outline, made a looksmaxxing obsession (2010s–2020s) for boys — a measure of worth God says He takes no pleasure in, beside the fear of Him that He does.

JAWLINE, n. (English; Gen Alpha / looksmaxxing usage, 2010s–present) The outline of the lower jaw, prized when sharp and square. "Bro’s jawline is insane."

Related: mewing, mogging, looksmaxxing, jawline check, jaw trainer.

Decode for parents: boys are being taught to grade their faces; ask what your son thinks of his.

Webster 1828, the root — JAW, n. The bones of the mouth in which the teeth are fixed.

Key Scripture

Psa 147:10 — "He delighteth not in the strength of the horse: he taketh not pleasure in the legs of a man."

Psa 147:11 — "The LORD taketh pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy."

Isa 53:2 — "For he shall grow up before him as a tender plant, and as a root out of a dry ground: he hath no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him."

1Ti 4:8 — "For bodily exercise profiteth little: but godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is, and of that which is to come."

Modern Corruption

The jawline fixation teaches boys that their worth is in the angle of their bones; Scripture says the LORD takes no pleasure in the legs of a man but in them that fear Him.

expand to see more

Looksmaxxing arrived in boys’ lives through edits, gym content, and online forums whose roots lie in incel culture, where the face is fate. The jawline is its central icon. Boys who absorb it begin to see themselves and others as faces to be ranked, and some fall into anxiety, compulsive mirror-checking, and despair over features they cannot change.

Answer with both care and truth. It is good for a boy to be strong, clean, and well-kept; it is ruinous for him to locate his worth in his jaw. Tell him often what you admire in his character, model contentment with your own aging face, and give him Psalm 147. The face God loves best is the one turned toward Him.

"He had no form nor comeliness — the face that saved the world (Isa 53:2)."
